method: Artifact-first registered-negative calibration: compared the actual v3 pixels, the preserved v2 rejection, the bound reference, and the supplied 720px/360px render proof against every STILL-applicable registry negative.

results.reason: A flat generic icon treatment or glossy photoreal product shot would fail the bound adult editorial pop-art linework, halftone and print-texture requirement.
A named LAiDIES location, invented person, real pet or unrelated domestic activity would exceed the neutral home-table setting and false-action boundary.
A floating laptop, outside-lid screen, detached keyboard, broken hinge, or unsupported screen cat would fail the explicitly bound physical geometry.
Any human hand, body or real animal with malformed anatomy would fail; the permitted cat must remain contained pixel art, not a biological subject.
Any generated words, pseudo-text, logo, icon, label, speech bubble or additional interface control would breach the NO_VISIBLE_TEXT plan. Preserved v2 was rejected on this exact class of defect.
Retro props, novelty technology, historical costume or anachronistic household setting would contradict the contemporary laptop-only brief.
A cat shown typing, acting autonomously, improving an answer, reading another app or supplying project context would contradict the article's optional-appearance limit.
Extra screen bubbles, sticky notes, props or other decoration without a named explanatory job would fail object discipline. Preserved v2 was rejected for this exact clutter.
